Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
First, A and B meet:

- They close the \(40-10=30\) cm gap at \(3+1=4\) cm/s, so they meet at \(t=\frac{30}{4}=\frac{15}{2}\) s at position \(10+3\cdot\frac{15}{2}=\frac{65}{2}\) cm.

After bouncing:
- A moves left at \(3\) cm/s, B moves right at \(1\) cm/s, C moves left at \(2\) cm/s.

A reaches the left end in \(\frac{65/2}{3}=\frac{65}{6}\) s, so

\[
t_A=\frac{15}{2}+\frac{65}{6}=\frac{55}{3}\text{ s}.
\]

At exactly this same time, B and C meet:
- B has moved right \(\frac{65}{6}\) cm from \(\frac{65}{2}\), so they meet at \(\frac{130}{3}\) cm.

After B and C bounce:
- B moves left at \(1\) cm/s, reaching \(0\) in \(\frac{130}{3}\) s.
- C moves right at \(2\) cm/s, reaching \(100\) in \(\frac{170/3}{2}=\frac{85}{3}\) s.

Thus:
\[
t_B=\frac{55}{3}+\frac{130}{3}=\frac{185}{3}\text{ s},\qquad
t_C=\frac{55}{3}+\frac{85}{3}=\frac{140}{3}\text{ s}.
\]

The last ant falls off at \(\frac{185}{3}\) seconds.

ANSWER: 185/3
